timeRange.note: Ischigualasto dinosaurs come from the Scaphonyx-Exaeretodon-Herrerasaurus biozone, dated by Martinez et al. (2011) to 231.5-229 Ma (late Carnian). PBDB places all occurrences in the Carnian.

lengthM.note: Single published figure (NHM Dino Directory); specimens vary in size.

summary.en: Herrerasaurus was one of the first big meat-eating dinosaurs. It hunted in what is now Argentina about 231 to 229 million years ago, when dinosaurs were still new. It ran on two legs and used short arms with sharp claws to grab prey. A complete skull and skeleton, described in 1992, helped scientists picture what the earliest dinosaurs looked like.

text.en: A complete skull and skeleton show Herrerasaurus was an agile two-legged predator with short arms built for grasping and raking.

uncertain.note: Where herrerasaurids sit in the dinosaur tree is unresolved. Sereno & Novas (1992) and Martinez et al. (2011) recover Herrerasaurus as a basal theropod; here Herrerasauridae is placed directly under Dinosauria.
No mass estimate found in a source we could verify.
